note: Two distinct things are bundled in the input name and they behave differently. (1) AARTI INDUSTRIES LTD — real, large, listed Indian chemical manufacturer; export shipments are CONFIRMED by dated customs/B-L rows with destination, HS code and B-L number (e.g. B/L 1138180 to St Louis USA, HS 29039130, 2026-02-28; B/L 1136904 to Qingdao China, HS 29049940; B/L 1141897 to Melbourne Australia, HS 29173940). (2) 'Ganesh Polychem (Special Resin division)' — ImportKey's page for slug /ganesh-polychem loads but returns an EMPTY record set: no shipment rows, no suppliers, no buyers, no totals. No trace of shipments under that name was found; it is not evidenced as a separate exporting entity. HS check against declared codes 290420;292142;292143;390730: the observed export rows carry 29039130, 29049940, 29173940, 29039990, 29202910 — i.e. benzene/chlorobenzene and phthalate derivatives, NOT the declared 290420 (nitro-toluene derivatives), 292142/292143 (aniline derivatives) or 390730 (epoxy resins). The declared HS set does not match the observed export lines; per project rule 3 this is NOT grounds for rejection — the company stays in the base and the code should be corrected to the factual codes actually shipped. Note also that the Jhagadia-page rows are imports (aniline, methanol, toluene feedstock), so that page alone would not prove exports; the Mulund-page rows are the export evidence. Revenue: quarterly revenue ₹2,627 Cr per company investor page; full-year figure and GST band not verified here — null rather than invented. No rejection grounds: entity exists and is actively trading.
